item.title: Scientists confirm global warming is accelerating faster than ever recorded

item.title: Livelihood, education goals affect migration under climate change
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — Climate-driven hazards can push many to leave their homes in search of a livelihood elsewhere, but aspirations for the future may change where they decide to migrate, according to a new study led by researchers at Penn State. At the same time, income losses due to climate shocks, or extreme weather events like floods or droughts, may constrain migration options for vulnerable populations.

item.title: Antarctica’s “Doomsday Glacier” could raise sea levels twice as much as predicted
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: global warming — Antarctica’s Thwaites Glacier may be melting twice as much as previously predicted, even without additional global warming. Scientists discovered that warm ocean water is penetrating miles beneath the ice, weakening its foundations and accelerating its retreat. A new model predicts that the glacier could add up to 30 millimeters to global sea levels by 2100, with a 60% chance of losing a crucial stabilizing ridge.

item.title: Researchers produce urea in the field using system powered by biobatteries and solar energy
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: renewable energy — The CONFETI project, coordinated by the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB), has concluded three years of research with the commissioning of a pilot system capable of producing urea, a nitrogen fertilizer widely used in agriculture, directly in the field using renewable energy. This fertilizer is produced from carbon dioxide (CO₂) and nitrates in an electrochemical reactor powered by energy from biobatteries and solar panels.
